articles.title: Fernando Mendoza enters the 2026 season chasing Jeremiyah Love in the Offensive Rookie of the Year race
articles.standfirst: Saquon Barkley was the last running back to win the award, in 2018
articles.summary: Saquon Barkley was the last running back to win the award, in 2018
articles.body:
The NFL preseason is officially heating up as Week 2 kicks off with the Las Vegas Raiders traveling to take on the Houston Texans . During their opening exhibition match against the Arizona Cardinals, rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza flashed his potential by completing 10 of 16 passes for 97 yards and a touchdown.

However, the front office and coaching staff plan to ease their prized rookie into action, slating veteran Kirk Cousins as the primary starter to begin the regular season.

Meanwhile, Arizona's rookie running back and third overall pick, Jeremiyah Love , made a massive first impression in that same 27-14 victory, rumbling for 58 rushing yards on heavy touches while adding three receptions to lead the team's backfield snaps.

The Early Betting Battle for Offensive Rookie of the Year

Looking ahead to the regular season, sportsbooks have installed both Mendoza and Love as the frontrunners for the Offensive Rookie of the Year award. Love currently holds the top spot at +500 odds , despite navigating a brutal schedule against powerhouse defenses from the NFC West (Rams, Seahawks, 49ers) and the AFC West (Chiefs, Chargers, Broncos, and Raiders).

Should Love capture the honor, he would become the first running back to win the award since Saquon Barkley dominated in 2018 by racking up 2,028 total yards (1,307 rushing) and 15 total touchdowns (11 rushing) .

Meanwhile, Mendoza sits closely behind at +550 odds , though his ultimate candidacy depends heavily on when he officially wrests the starting job away from Cousins.

If he secures the role early, Mendoza aims to follow in the footsteps of recent history as just the third quarterback in four years to claim the award, following wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan , who took home the hardware last season.

Chasing the Frontrunners: Rising Stars Eyeing the Rookie Crown

Tied right behind the top favorites at +600 odds is Love's former teammate at Notre Dame, Jadarian Price . The dynamic running back was selected in the first round by the defending champion Seattle Seahawks , where he is expected to fill the void left by Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III while sharing a backfield with Zach Charbonnet , who continues working his way back from injury.

Sharing those same +600 odds is explosive wideout Carnell Tate , the fourth overall pick who arrived in Tennessee to bolster Cam Ward's receiving corps.

Working alongside established veterans like Calvin Ridley and Wan'Dale Robinson under new offensive coordinator Brian Daboll , Tate is primed for an immediate, high-volume role that could easily vault him to the top of the rookie leaderboards before winter arrives.

articles.title: Matt Leinart embarrassed by how he ruined Rihanna date and landed in the 'friendzone'
articles.summary: Matt Leinart enjoyed plenty of high-pressure moments during his football career, but apparently none prepared him for going on a date with Rihanna.
articles.body:
Matt Leinart enjoyed plenty of high-pressure moments during his football career, but apparently none prepared him for going on a date with Rihanna .

The former Arizona Cardinals quarterback has opened up about the encounter, admitting a combination of nerves and insecurity left him unable to make the impression he wanted.

“Oh God, are we really going there?” Leinart said when the subject was raised on The Dan Patrick Show.

“I wasn’t at my best,” Leinart admitted. “I definitely wasn’t at my best that day. We were friends, we hung out a couple times, we had a mutual circle of friends, and her assistant and sort of right-hand girl, still to this day I’m friends with, she grew up with one of my best friends, so that was kind of the thing.”

Leinart's confidence disappeared on Rihanna date

Leinart and Rihanna had already become friends through their shared social circle before agreeing to meet at Teddy's nightclub inside the Hollywood Roosevelt Hotel.

However, Leinart previously explained on his Throwbacks podcast that a large blister appeared on his lip at precisely the wrong time.

“The problem was I had this f****ng ginormous blister on my lip,” Leinart said.

The problem affected his confidence far more than he expected, with the former quarterback comparing his embarrassment to insecurities he experienced as a child.

“I would get these sun blisters,” he explained. “I felt like when I used to be super fat when I was little, and I was afraid to take my shirt off at P.E. You know, when you’re so embarrassed you’re like, ‘Please don’t look at me.’”

Matt Leinart admits he couldn't even make eye contact

Friends convinced Leinart to go through with the date despite his concerns, but the discomfort didn't disappear once he arrived.

“I couldn’t make eye contact, dude,” Leinart recalled, describing how difficult he found simply talking to Rihanna .

Looking back, Leinart believes his younger self simply lacked the confidence people might have expected from a successful NFL quarterback.

“But yeah, it was a young Matt , not super confident,” Leinart said. “You thought I would have had a lot of confidence; I didn’t, and yeah, so that’s that.”

There was ultimately no second date, leaving Leinart with a memorable story about the night his chance with one of the world's biggest music stars ended firmly in friendship.

articles.title: Cardinals star misses out on massive $285,000 bonus due to strict contract clause: What happened?
articles.standfirst: Jacoby Brissett can earn a massive weekly bonus, but only when his playing time ends with a victory
articles.summary: Jacoby Brissett can earn a massive weekly bonus, but only when his playing time ends with a victory
articles.body:
Jacoby Brissett didn't just leave Seattle with one of his poorest statistical performances in recent memory. The Arizona Cardinals quarterback also missed out on a potential $285,000 payday because of an unusual incentive buried in his contract.

Brissett ’s one-year deal reportedly includes a clause that awards him $285,000 whenever he plays at least 50 percent of Arizona’s offensive snaps and the Cardinals win. That second requirement proved decisive in Week 2.

Arizona’s offense struggled badly against the Seahawks , with Brissett throwing for only 95 yards while completing 60.7 percent of his passes. He finished with one touchdown and one interception as the Cardinals were overwhelmed after an encouraging opening weekend.

The contrast with Week 1 was considerable. Brissett had thrown for 277 yards and a touchdown while completing 73 percent of his passes in Arizona’s 26-14 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers , playing enough snaps and securing the win needed to trigger the incentive.

Brissett can earn millions

The weekly bonus forms part of a reworked one-year agreement worth $15.5 million guaranteed, with incentives capable of pushing its total value to approximately $21 million.

Brissett can reportedly collect the $285,000 win incentive up to 10 times. If he satisfies the conditions on all 10 occasions, that portion alone would be worth $2.85 million.

The structure gives Arizona flexibility while offering Brissett a significant financial reward if he stays on the field and leads the Cardinals to victories. Week 2 showed how quickly that money can disappear.

Seattle’s defense prevented Arizona from developing any rhythm, while the Cardinals ’ running game offered little support. Rookie Jeremiyah Love finished with only 29 yards on nine carries.

Seattle had no such problems offensively. Drew Lock threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba catching all three scores as part of a 155-yard performance.

Pressure builds before another difficult matchup

Brissett now gets an immediate opportunity to recover when Arizona faces the San Francisco 49ers .

The Cardinals entered the season viewing the veteran as a short-term starter rather than a long-term answer, and rookie Carson Beck remains behind him on the depth chart.

There's no indication that Arizona is preparing an immediate change, but the nature of Brissett ’s contract means the team has little long-term financial reason to remain committed if the offense continues to struggle.

His Week 1 showing demonstrated that Mike LaFleur ’s system can produce results with Brissett at quarterback. Week 2 raised the opposite possibility.

Each start will now carry two separate stakes: Arizona’s position in the NFC West and Brissett’s own earning potential. Playing enough snaps gets him halfway there. Winning is what unlocks the money.
